title: Uniform continuity on a compact metric subset
statement:
Let $(X,d_X)$ and $(Y,d_Y)$ be metric spaces. Let $C\subseteq X$ be compact, meaning every open cover has a finite subcover, and let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous on $C$ with its subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. Then $f$ is uniformly continuous on $C$: for every $\epsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that
$$x,y\in C,\quad d_X(x,y)<\delta\quad\Longrightarrow\quad d_Y(f(x),f(y))<\epsilon.$$
The empty set is allowed; completeness of either metric space is not required.
